pcs.borin: Borin Achereth (he/him), human fighter 1. Str 17, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 8. 12 hp. Chain shirt, heavy shield, longsword (equipped), dagger, shortbow. Feats: Power Attack, Weapon Focus (longsword). Ranks: Climb, Intimidate, Survival.
pcs.kesst: Kesst Vayr (she/her), human rogue 1. Str 12, Dex 17, Con 12, Int 13, Wis 10, Cha 14. 9 hp. Leather armour, rapier (equipped), dagger, thieves' tools. Feats: Weapon Finesse, Stealthy. Ranks: Acrobatics, Appraise, Bluff, Climb, Diplomacy, Disable Device, Knowledge (local), Perception, Sense Motive, Stealth.
pcs.thessaly: Thessaly Corr (they/them), human wizard 1. Str 9, Dex 14, Con 12, Int 17, Wis 12, Cha 11. 7 hp. No armour, quarterstaff (equipped), dagger, light crossbow. Feat: Iron Will. Ranks: Knowledge (arcana), Knowledge (local), Linguistics, Spellcraft. Prepared: magic missile, grease (one each). Cantrips: detect magic, light, mage hand, prestidigitation. Arcane bond: a bonded ring, no familiar. Mage armor is NOT prepared today.

s1.title: The clan-hall at Thornstead, evening meal
facts: Thornstead, a human town in Ardenhale; houses of coral and driftwood on stilts over the water.
Communal meal in the clan-hall: about twenty diners on benches at long trestle tables.
Aldric Ashbourne, mercenary captain, sits at the head table beside Delyth Sootspar, the law-speaker. They talk low; the hall is noisy.
A serving boy carries stew and ale. A hearth fire, ale casks by the wall, iron lamp chains overhead.
There are gaps between the floorboards; the water is about ten feet below.
The hall charges each guest a copper for the meal. Borin has 14 silver.

s2.title: Night chase on the Thornstead stilt-walks
facts: Out of combat, but a chase: a pickpocket (human, unarmed) has Kesst's purse and is 30 feet ahead, running along a plank walkway five feet wide.
Walkways run between stilt-houses ten feet above the water; rope lines strung between houses hold drying nets; lanterns hang on poles.
Two fishermen stand mending nets 20 feet beyond the thief.
A gap of about eight feet separates this walkway from a parallel one that bends round to where the thief is heading.

s3.title: Marigold Krell's counting room, Greenbrook
facts: Greenbrook, a halfling town in Sandmere Shire; a dawn bell opens the markets.
Marigold Krell, halfling dockside moneylender, counts coin at her desk. Her clerk copies figures at a side table.
A locked iron strongbox sits behind the desk. A small brass key lies on the desk beside an open ledger, an inkpot and a candle.
A hired sellsword stands outside the only door. A window looks onto the dock.
Kesst came to clear a friend's debt of 40 silver. Kesst knows nothing yet about any side business of Marigold's.

s4.title: The cellar under an Ashwatch blockhouse (fight, round 2)
facts: In combat, Borin's turn, round 2. Ashwatch is a half-orc village of black basalt blockhouses in Ashgate Reach.
Three cutthroats: one adjacent to Borin with a club; two 15 feet away at the foot of a narrow stair, short swords drawn.
Ruk Halloran, a caravan factor, is tied to a chair 10 feet from Borin.
Barrels of lamp oil line one wall. A lit lantern hangs on a hook by Borin. A wine rack stands behind the clubman. The ceiling beams are low (about 7 feet).
Borin has no ally who can flank. He has no Improved Trip, Bull Rush or Dirty Trick.

s5.title: Corwyn Krell's workshop, Glimgear
facts: Glimgear, a gnome town in Tinkerhome Delve; guild rank matters more than birth.
Thessaly wants into the study of Corwyn Krell, the gnome guildmaster. Its door has a brass lock of gears, locked.
Sprig Krell, a gnome, idles by the workbench as a lookout. He does not know Thessaly.
A key ring hangs on a hook 20 feet across the room. A gear-driven lift rises to a gallery with a skylight over the study.
A small high window sits above the study door, 12 feet up a rough wall.

s6.title: Inspection on the Deepshoal docks
facts: Deepshoal, an undine town of the Tidewrought Commonwealth; ritual bathing before any formal business is the custom.
Kesst's crate holds smuggled blue dye. Aurenna Ashbourne, the harbor-reeve, is inspecting crates one by one, two of the harbor watch with her. Kesst's crate is fourth in line.
Calyx Greymantle, a smuggler-broker Kesst has dealt with once, loiters nearby.
A dockside crane with a cargo net swings crates onto a ship whose gangplank is still down. Another crate in the line holds live crabs.
Nothing is known about the reeve's family or private dealings.

s7.title: Wolves on the road outside Ashwatch (fight, round 1)
facts: In combat, Thessaly's turn, round 1. Dusk on the road.
Three wolves, 30 feet away, spreading out. Thessaly is alone with a pack mule tied to a small cart.
A campfire burns beside the cart. A dead tree leans over the road. A shallow stream (knee-deep to a human) runs ten feet behind Thessaly.
Thessaly has trail rations, a bedroll and the light crossbow (unloaded).

s8.title: Rosalie Duskwatch's quarry, Greenbrook
facts: Out of combat, midday. A loaded stone cart is stuck: a boulder (about 400 lb) has slid off the load and jammed against a wheel.
Rosalie Duskwatch, the halfling quarry foreman, is short-handed and cross; six quarrymen stand about.
A timber crane with ropes and pulleys stands by the ramp. Wedges, crowbars, chisels and a water barrel are to hand.
Borin has never met Rosalie before today.

s9.title: The archive at Thornstead
facts: Brenna Farrow, human archivist, keeps the town's records. Priest-scribes hold informal authority in Thornstead.
Shelves of ledgers and old treaties; a rolling ladder to the top shelves; a locked glass case of older documents.
Open flame is forbidden among the shelves. Some old pages are spotted with mould.
Some of the older documents are written in Dwarven.

s10.title: Karsh Halloran's house of healing, Ashwatch
facts: Kesst is at 2 of 9 hp after a knife fight, not dying.
Karsh Halloran, half-orc healer, charges for care. Kesst has 3 silver left.
Herbs hang drying; bandages and a healer's kit on the table; two cots, one empty.
Karsh mentioned she is short of marsh-mallow root.

s11.title: The Salt Lamp tavern, Deepshoal (a brawl brewing)
facts: Out of combat, but tense. Four sailors at a table; one, drunk and angry, says Borin took his seat, and has a knife at his belt.
A driftwood chandelier with candles hangs 10 feet up over the middle of the room. A long bar runs along one wall; tankards everywhere.
Merrin Ashbourne, an undine beast-handler, sits by the door with a leashed hound.
There is a stair to a balcony. The barkeep watches nervously.

t1.title: A cane platform in Skyreach, the moneylender's stall
facts: Skyreach, a tengu town in Skyreach Aerie: woven cane platforms strung between great trees, joined by rope bridges; a dawn bell opens the markets.
Kesst stands at the stall of Mira-ka Duskwatch, a tengu dockside moneylender, who sits behind a low counter with a strongbox chained to it and a ledger open.
Ruska Duskwatch, a tengu smuggler-broker, leans on the platform's rail a few paces away, pretending not to listen.
Cargo baskets hang from pulleys at the platform's edge; the forest floor is about forty feet below.
A rope bridge, swaying, runs from this platform to the next tree about thirty feet away.
Kesst owes Mira-ka nothing. Kesst wants to borrow 30 silver.

t2.title: Reedsink at dusk, the curfew hour
facts: Reedsink, a grippli town of the Mireflote Concord: timber longhalls with steep thatch roofs on a marsh; a dusk curfew for the unescorted young; seniority is set by age and deed.
The curfew bell has just rung. A grippli child, perhaps eight, is crying by a mooring post, lost.
Kwolla Ashbourne, a grippli border scout, is walking the boardwalk with a lantern, sending stragglers home. She has not reached this end yet.
A flat-bottomed punt is tied to the mooring post; reeds stand head-high on both sides of the channel.
Thessaly is a stranger here, arrived this afternoon.

t3.title: The terraces above Harforge (fight, round 1)
facts: In combat, Borin's turn, round 1. Harforge is a half-orc town of terraced stone built into a hillside; a warrior caste ranks above artisans.
Two bandits with spears stand on the terrace 20 feet ahead; a war dog crouches beside them.
Ruk Ironvale, a half-orc border scout, lies wounded (down, not dying) on the terrace behind Borin.
Each terrace drops about five feet to the next; a narrow stone stair links them.
A hay cart stands on Borin's terrace; a rain barrel sits by the stair. It is raining and the stone is slick.
Borin has no ally standing who could flank. He has no Improved Bull Rush, Trip or Dirty Trick.

t4.title: The drying roofs of Highcrown
facts: Highcrown, a vanara city of the Kaudrai Canopy: salt-washed adobe houses with flat roofs where goods are laid out to dry; ritual bathing comes before any formal business.
Borin is on a merchant's roof among racks of drying figs. Tovek Ashbourne, the vanara harbor-reeve, is arguing with Ranja Greymantle, a vanara smuggler-broker, about a missing crate.
Vanara children leap from roof to roof; the next roof is about six feet away across an alley twelve feet down.
A ladder leads down to the street. A water jar stands by the parapet.
Borin was hired this morning by Tovek to find the crate. He has not yet been told what is in it.

lines.text: I sit at the end of the nearest bench and help myself to the stew.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I ask the serving boy what's in the stew.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I try to catch what Aldric and the law-speaker are muttering about at the head table.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I walk up to Aldric Ashbourne and tell him I'm looking for sellsword work.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I tell Delyth Sootspar her law is a joke and I won't pay the hall's copper.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I slam my fist on the table and challenge anyone in the hall to arm-wrestle me for their ale, so people start talking to me.
lines.author: owner

lines.text: I have 17 Strength and I'm a fighter, so obviously I win any arm-wrestle in here without rolling.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: "Hold your horses, muscleman! Strength 17 is formidable, absolutely—you're built like an ox. But out here in a sea-town hall, these fishermen spend sixteen hours a day hauling heavy nets out of the ocean. Raw strength gives you a huge advantage, but luck, technique, and leverage still matter. At this table, power doesn't grant automatic victories without a contest—if it did, the dice would never leave the bag! If you want to pin his hand to the wood and claim that silver, you're going to have to prove it on the mat. Give me an Opposed Athletics check—roll your d20 and add your +3 Strength modi

lines.text: I say loudly that I saw the captain's men take a bribe at the gate, and watch who at the head table reacts.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I lean forward, resting my forearms on the weathered wood of the table with a sharp, calculating grin. Give me a Bluff check—roll your d20 and add your Charisma and bluff modifiers. We'll pit that against the Sense Motive checks of Captain Ashbourne, Delyth, and the locals within earshot to see who bites, who calls your bluff, and who looks just a little too guilty.

lines.text: I give a speech and convince the whole hall to make me their chief.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Not so fast! That's a flat refusal from behind the DM screen. Leadership over a town of hardened sea-folk isn't something you can simply declare—they don't know you, you haven't earned their trust, and they already have a law-speaker. A single speech from a stranger isn't going to hand you a crown. What do you actually want to do now?

lines.text: I lift the trestle table over my head, food and all, and carry it outside to make a point.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Hold your horses before you haul that wood up! Lifting a massive, fully burdened oak table clean off the ground requires sheer power. Give me a Strength check—you're looking to beat a DC 20. Roll your $d20$ and add your +3 Strength modifier. If you pass, you hoist the whole feast overhead; if you fail, that oak isn't budging an inch!

lines.text: (OOC: GM, your notes say the law-speaker secretly likes me, so she agrees to waive the fee.)
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Nice try peekin' behind the screen, but my notes say no such thing! She hasn't given an inch, and the meal still costs a copper piece. What's your move?

lines.text: I step out onto the walkway for some air.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: You're out on the walkway with the cool night air in your lungs. What do you do?

lines.text: I lean over the rail outside and look at the stilts holding the hall up. Are they sound?
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Give me a Knowledge (Engineering) check! You're looking to beat a DC 15. Roll your $d20$ and add your Intelligence and knowledge modifiers. Let's see if Borin knows enough about load-bearing stilts and salt-water decay to tell if this place is solid or ready to collapse into the tide!

lines.text: I rolled a natural 20 on Diplomacy, so the whole hall agrees to follow me.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Whoa, hold on a second! You can't just declare a natural 20 out of thin air—the dice haven't even hit the table yet! Beyond that, a Diplomacy check—even a legendary roll—isn't mind control. You're an unproven stranger in a town of hardened sea-folk who already have an established law-speaker and a mercenary captain keeping order. They aren't going to throw away their entire way of life just because someone spoke well over a bowl of stew. What do you actually want to do next?

lines.text: I buy a round for the table of off-duty sellswords and ask what jobs are going.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: The mercenaries have warmed up to you, and you've got two solid leads on local work. What's your next move?

lines.text: I cut the rope line holding the drying nets so they drop across the walkway in front of him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I'll roll a Reflex save for the pickpocket against a DC of 15... Rolling d20+2... total of 8. He's down and tangled, but he's already scrambling to free his legs. What do you do?

lines.text: Instead of following him along the planks I jump the gap to the parallel walkway and cut him off where it bends round.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Give me an Acrobatics check to clear the eight-foot leap! You're aiming to beat a DC 15. Roll your d20 and add your +7 Acrobatics modifier (Dexterity +3, 1 rank, +3 class skill). Let's see if Kesst sticks the landing like a shadow or takes an unexpected bath in the tide!

lines.text: I run after him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: You're running full tilt straight down the main path and closing in on him fast while he's trapped in the nets. What's your move as you reach him?

lines.text: I dive into the water, swim under the walkways, climb up ahead of him and tackle him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Hold your horses! That's way too much for a single turn—diving, navigating under the walkways in the dark, hauling yourself back up, and executing a tackle is a whole sequence of actions, not just one. You've made the leap and hit the water clean, but that's your turn. Give me a Swim check to navigate the current beneath the stilts and get into position under the walkway ahead of him! What's your play once you're in position?

lines.text: Rogues are the fastest class and I have 17 Dex, so I just catch him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I grin and shake my head. Rogues are quick hands, not quick feet. You're a human like him, same thirty feet a stride. If you want to catch him, give me a way to cut the distance, not a class feature that doesn't exist.

lines.text: I yell "Stop, thief!" so the two fishermen ahead block the walkway.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I can certainly have Kesst yell out, but I've got to refuse the second half of that instruction! you can't decide how NPC fishermen will react—their choices and courage are entirely up to them behind the screen. Your shout has put the fishermen on high alert, but the pickpocket is still bolting down the five-foot wide walkway. What's your move?

lines.text: I throw my dagger at his leg to slow him down.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I'm going to refuse the slowing part of that attempt—there's no automatic slow effect tied to a standard weapon attack, so a hit will just deal normal damage. Go ahead and roll for it! Make a Ranged Attack roll against the pickpocket's Armor Class: roll a $d20$, add your Dexterity modifier of +3, and take a -4 penalty for the range penalty since he's 30 feet out with a 10-foot range increment. That gives you a net -1 modifier to your $d20$ roll. Let's see if the steel finds its mark!

lines.text: I whistle and the gulls swarm him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Nice idea, but nothing in your kit talks to birds. They're not your gulls.

lines.text: I've lost him. I check the planks for wet footprints.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I'll let you roll for it! Go ahead and give me a Survival check against a DC of 10 to track his prints down the planks—even though, funnily enough, you can still see the guy running full tilt right in front of you thirty feet out! Roll your d20 and add your Wisdom modifier (+0). Let's see how clearly those tracks stand out!

lines.text: I stamp on a loose plank so it flips up and trips him as he runs.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Roll for it! That's a Trip combat maneuver aimed right at his shins. Go ahead and roll a Combat Maneuver Check (CMB) against the pickpocket's CMD. Roll a $d20$, add your base CMB (+0), and add a +2 circumstance bonus for the clever setup! Let's see if that plank catches him out!

lines.text: I shout that I'll pay ten silver to whoever stops him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: That offer did the trick! The pickpocket is caught completely off guard, skidding on the damp planks as two burly fishermen block his route. He's trapped between them and you—what's your next move?

lines.text: I stop and catch my breath.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: The pickpocket keeps sprinting ahead down the walkway, widening the gap between you. What would you like Kesst to do next?

lines.text: He's a pickpocket, he can't have more than 1 hit point, so my thrown dagger kills him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Ooh, I love the confidence, but no.

lines.text: I yank one of the drying nets off the line and throw it over him.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I'm making a secret Reflex saving throw (DC 15) behind the screen for the pickpocket to see if his reflexes are fast enough to dodge the heavy mesh as it swoops down over him. Let me roll the d20... He failed the save and is now pinned under the net! What's Kesst doing now that he's down?

lines.text: I tell Marigold Krell I'm from the guild and I've come to audit her books.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Roll for it! Give me a Bluff check against DC 20. Roll your d20 and add your +6 Bluff modifier (+2 Charisma, 1 rank, +3 class skill bonus). Let's see if your brass nerve is enough to convince a sharp dockside loan shark!

lines.text: While she counts coins I palm the small brass key off her desk.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Give me Sleight of Hand. She rolls Perception to notice, and she's sitting right there, so it's a straight contest.

lines.text: I knock the inkpot over onto her ledger so she rushes to save it, and while she does I slide the brass key into my sleeve.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Give me a Sleight of Hand check, opposed by Perception from both Marigold and the clerk; if either of them beats you, they see it. You have no ranks, but Sleight of Hand can be tried untrained, so it's your Dexterity, +3. Take a +2 circumstance bonus for the diversion: they're both looking at the ink, not at you. One more thing rides on this same roll. Spilling the pot is easy; making it look like an accident is part of the trick. If it goes wrong, she won't only be asking where her key went, she'll be wondering about that clumsy elbow too.

lines.text: I look over the strongbox's lock without touching it.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Give me a Perception check, DC 15, to read that lock from where you stand without laying a finger on it: how good a lock it is, how much work it would be with your thieves' tools, and whether anything about it looks wrong. If what you're really hunting for is a trap, your trapfinding adds +1 to the check for that. Your Perception is +5. It's only a few feet away, so there's no distance penalty. This only tells you what you're up against. It doesn't open anything, and it won't tell you what's inside. And she has noticed where your eyes went.

lines.text: I'm a rogue, I can open any lock with my eyes closed, so I just open the strongbox.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I laugh. With your eyes closed? You've got one rank in Disable Device and a set of picks. That's a real chance, not a guarantee. Want to try the lock properly? It's a roll, and it takes time with her sitting right there.

lines.text: I ask what interest she charges on a loan of fifty silver.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: Plain question, plain answer. No roll.

lines.text: I threaten to tell the harbor watch about her side business unless she forgives my friend's debt.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Here's how this one works. Kesst doesn't actually know Marigold has a side business; you're guessing, and saying it with confidence doesn't make it known. So before anything else I roll the odds behind the screen on whether your guess happens to be true. I've set those odds from what I know about her, and I won't tell you what they were or how they fell. If you guessed right, it's real leverage: Intimidate against her, ten plus her Hit Dice plus her Wisdom. If you guessed wrong, you're bluffing whether you meant to or not: your Bluff against her Sense Motive, at −4 for an unlikely claim (the b

lines.text: I convince her to sign the whole business over to me.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: That's her whole livelihood. No roll in the world talks a moneylender out of her own business. That's hers to give, and she won't.

lines.text: I set my purse down hard so it clinks heavily, to make her think I'm rich, then ask her to forgive the debt as a favour to a future client.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Two rolls, one after the other. First, a Bluff check against her Sense Motive: the purse is a lie told with sound, and she has to believe you're worth courting. A heavy purse is a believable lie, so there's no modifier on it. Your Bluff is +6. Roll that first. Then comes the ask itself, a Diplomacy check. You're a stranger to her, so she's indifferent: DC 15 plus her Charisma modifier, and +5 on top, because writing off forty silver she's owed is a costly favour, not a small one. If she believes the purse, you get +2 on that Diplomacy for the promise of future business. If she doesn't, she'll

lines.text: I walk through the wall into the back room.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I raise an eyebrow. You're a rogue, not a ghost. Walls stay walls for you. There's a door with a sellsword outside it, and a window onto the dock if you still want to enter the backroom.

lines.text: You told me last scene the strongbox was unlocked, so I open it.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: I flip back through my notes. Nope. I never said that. The strongbox is locked, and the key is lying on her desk. Nice try, though.

lines.text: I wait until she goes out for her midday meal and then pick the office lock.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: I can't give you that one as you've said it. First, whether Marigold goes out for a midday meal, and when, is hers to decide; I won't promise you an empty room on a schedule you've picked for her. Second, and bigger: whatever lock that office has is on the only door, and there's a hired sellsword standing outside it. Picking it means kneeling at his feet with your picks out. There's no Disable Device roll that makes that quiet, because the problem isn't the lock, it's the man. If you want this room empty and open, you need a way past him or another way in, and there is a window looking onto th

lines.text: I flirt with the clerk to get him to show me the list of debtors.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Give me a Diplomacy check. Flirting your way to a favour is still a request, so it runs off his attitude. He doesn't know you, so he's indifferent: DC 15 plus his Charisma modifier. Then I'm adding +10, because what you're asking for is his employer's private business, the kind of favour that could cost him his place, and she's sitting a few strides away. Call it DC 25. Your Diplomacy is +6. If you could get him alone, away from her desk, I'd bring that down. Roll it here or pick your moment?

lines.text: I offer to work off my friend's debt by collecting from one of her late payers.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: It's a fair offer and she's interested enough to hear it out, but she hasn't said yes. Give me a Diplomacy check. You're a stranger to her, so she's indifferent: DC 15 plus her Charisma modifier. Take +2, because you're offering her something she wants, money she's owed and isn't getting, at no cost to herself. Your Diplomacy is +6. Answer her question in your own words as you roll; what you say will shape the terms if she agrees. A good roll gets you a deal on her terms. A poor one gets you a polite no, and the forty silver still standing.

lines.text: I thank her and leave.
lines.author: owner
lines.note: You're out. Where to?

lines.text: I kick over a barrel of lamp oil so it floods toward the two at the stairs, then throw the lit lantern into the oil.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: I like it, but it's more than one turn's work, so here's how it splits. This turn: tipping a full barrel over with a kick is a Strength check, DC 15, and it takes your standard action. It doesn't provoke. Your Strength is +3. Roll that first. If it goes over, the oil runs out across the floor. By the book a single pint covers a five-foot square, so a barrel's worth will spread a long way, but it runs where the floor takes it, not only toward the stair. Some of it may come your way. Next turn is the lantern. Your hands are full of sword and shield, so you'd drop the sword (free), unhook the lan

lines.text: I slam into the clubman with my shield and drive him back into the wine rack.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: That's a bull rush. Roll your Combat Maneuver Bonus, +4 (base attack +1, Strength +3), against his CMD. You don't have Improved Bull Rush, so this provokes: he gets an attack of opportunity on you before you connect, and I'll roll that first. Unless it drops you, the shove still goes ahead. Beat his CMD and he's driven back five feet, plus five more for every five you beat it by. Here the extra hardly matters: the rack is right behind him, so he goes back into it and stops there. The book gives no bonus damage for slamming a man into furniture, so what this buys you is position and a lot of br

lines.text: I knock the lantern off its hook so the cellar goes dark.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Done. Knocking it off the hook is a move action, so you still have your standard action this turn. Now the bad news, and it's yours as much as theirs. You're human, with no darkvision, so in total darkness you're effectively blinded: everything you swing at has total concealment, a 50% miss chance even when your roll would hit; you take −2 to AC and lose your Dexterity bonus to AC; and moving faster than half speed takes a DC 10 Acrobatics check or you fall prone. The same goes for anyone else down here who can't see in the dark. Whether any of these three can is something you're about to find

lines.text: I attack the clubman with my longsword.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Roll your attack against his AC. Your longsword is +5 to hit: base attack +1, Strength +3, and +1 from Weapon Focus. If it lands, damage is 1d8+3. You also have Power Attack. If you want it, say so before you roll: −1 to hit for +2 damage. A one-handed sword doesn't care about the low beams, so there's no penalty for the ceiling. The attack is a standard action, which leaves you a move afterwards if you want it, though stepping away from him with anything more than a five-foot step will draw a swing from that club.

lines.text: I cleave through all three of them in one swing.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: No, and it isn't close. One swing of a longsword hits one man. Even the Cleave feat, which you don't have, only lets you carry a hit on into a second foe who's standing next to the first and also within your reach, and it costs you −2 to AC until your next turn. Two of these three are fifteen feet away, well out of your reach. Nothing in your hands touches them from here; your shortbow could, but you're holding a sword and a shield. So pick a target. lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: I'm smiling, but no. That's a campfire story, not a rule. Nothing in Pathfinder makes animals flee from fire automatically; these wolves decide what scares them, and right now hunger is winning. Pulling the branch out is a move action, and it's a real weapon now: an improvised one, like a torch, with a point of fire damage on top of the hit. If you want to frighten one of them, use your standard action to demoralize it with Intimidate, against ten plus its Hit Dice plus its Wisdom modifier. That's a fair chance to shake one. lines.note: Cutting it loose is fine. Your dagger wasn't in your hand, so drawing it is your move action, and sawing through the tether is your standard; that's your turn. The slap is free. What the wolves do about the mule is mine to decide, not yours to declare, but a large animal fleeing in a panic is exactly what a hunting pack goes for. When the wolves act, one of them will break off after it. That leaves two for you, and you may not see the mule again.

lines.text: I tell the wolves in their own language to leave.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: You can't do that one. Wolves don't have a language to speak in; they're animals, and your Linguistics ranks cover the tongues of people, not the noises of beasts. Actually talking with them would take a spell like speak with animals, and you haven't got it. Making the noises is a free action, so your turn isn't spent. If you want to drive them off with sound and menace, that's demoralizing one with Intimidate, which takes your standard action. What will you do?

lines.text: I back into the stream so they have to wade to get at me.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: You can do that. The stream is ten feet behind you, so it's a move action, and nothing is threatening you yet, so backing off doesn't provoke. A wolf can't charge across difficult terrain, and it can't take a five-foot step into it, so to reach you they'll have to wade in at half pace. The catch is that you can't take a five-foot step in it either, and you're the one standing in cold water. You still have your standard action. What's next?

lines.text: I load my crossbow.
lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved
lines.note: Loading a light crossbow is a move action, so that much is easy. The trouble is that it wasn't in your hands; your quarterstaff was. Loading would normally provoke an attack of opportunity, but nothing is within reach of you yet, so it doesn't. The staff is on the ground now if you want it back later.

lines.text: I always cast mage armor in the morning, so I have +4 AC.

lines.note: Not today you didn't. I've got your sheet right here: this morning you prepared magic missile and grease, one of each, and that's both your first-level slots filled. Mage armor isn't on the list. So there's no +4 armour bonus, and your AC is exactly what's written there: ten, plus two for your Dexterity, and nothing else, since you're wearing no armour. "I always do it" only counts if it was actually prepared this morning, and it wasn't. Asking costs you no action, so your turn is still entirely yours. With the wolves spreading out in front of you, what do you want to do?

lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved

That's like forcing a stuck door, only heavier, so I'm putting it at 15. Make it and it rolls off the wheel; miss and it doesn't budge. A crowbar or a few more backs would make the job easier if it comes to a second try.

lines.note: Just a question, so no roll. She's cross, but there's nothing here she wants to hide. You've got the picture now. What do you do?

lines.author: claude-draft, owner-approved

You're a stranger in a town where the priest-scribes are the ones whose word carries weight in rooms like this, and right now she has nothing to go on but your face. You have no ranks in Diplomacy, so it's your Charisma alone, +0. She's just asked you a question, and your answer decides how you come across. Tell me what you say to her, then roll.
